A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same PLAN-AND-ACT study. Their text, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison. Appendix A.1–A.10 is retained unchanged; v3 adds A.11–A.12.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebArena-Lite experiments comparing planner/executor configurations, synthetic-data augmentation and dynamic replanning, particularly in Table 1.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original CoT and model-size results, WebArena and WebVoyager evaluations, and website-level performance analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 3.4 and 4.2.2 add a CoT training/inference extension, including teacher-generated action rationales and reasoning before plans/actions. The two-agent architecture, grounded-plan generation and dynamic replanning remain intact. v1 already included planner Reasoning fields in its appendix; the extension particularly changes executor reasoning and its supervision.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only WebArena-Lite's simulated web tasks. v3 additionally trains and evaluates on WebVoyager's dynamic, real-world websites (Section 5.5), substantially extending the represented data and environmental conditions.

E2.justification: Within WebArena-Lite, Table 1 adds GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, AWM + GPT-4-0613 and WebPilot + GPT-4o to the retained comparisons. Tables 3–4 additionally include NNetNav, AutoWebGLM, AgentOccam variants, OpenWebVoyager, WebVoyager variants, Wilbur and Agent-E. These are reported numerical comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: v3 adds full-WebArena evaluation and 8B/32B model configurations alongside the original 70B experiments. The new WebVoyager training setup uses 1,500 synthetic trajectories and 10,000 synthetic plans. Appendix A.11 adds step-count metrics separated by success/failure. The original WebArena-Lite settings remain; newly disclosed hyperparameters do not establish changes to those settings.

E4.justification: Tables 1–2 add a focused CoT comparison and examine whether smaller CoT models approach the non-CoT 70B model. Appendix A.11 adds website-level success rates and action-length analysis by outcome. The earlier augmentation ablations, replanning examples and failure classifications are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3 continues point-estimate reporting; its additional average step counts do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 scores remain, including 53.94% for dynamic replanning. v3 adds 57.58% for the CoT variant, smaller-model results, and new benchmark results, including QWQ-32B's 48.15% on WebArena and 81.36% on WebVoyager. Appendix A.11 adds website and step-count results. Section 5.3.2's stated 4.36% CoT gain conflicts with Table 1's 3.64-percentage-point difference.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations. The added CoT material concerns an empirical training and inference procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the headline empirical claim from approximately 54% success on WebArena-Lite to 57.58% there and a text-only state-of-the-art 81.36% on WebVoyager, extending claimed success to real-world web tasks. The architectural and synthetic-data contributions remain. The introduction's 53.94% contribution bullet and conclusion are not fully updated.

C2.justification: A new Limitations section identifies dependence on a capable trajectory-collection model when training data are unavailable and the efficiency cost of replanning after every action. Section 5.3.2 also interprets the smaller-model comparison as evidence for CoT's importance. Earlier interpretations concerning plan quality, overfitting and dynamic content remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.12/Figure 5 supplies previously absent training and inference specifications, including learning rate, optimizer, batch size, epochs, 8×A100 hardware, software frameworks and decoding limits. Section 5.1 identifies the CoT teacher and specifies five seed examples per ten generated examples; Section 5.5 documents WebVoyager collection and annotation models. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially expands positioning against hierarchical planning methods, including AgentOccam, WebPilot, AdaPlanner and ADaPT, and discusses complementary trajectory-generation approaches and robotic planners. It explicitly distinguishes the work through trainable models, architectural simplicity and synthetic planning data. Additional references support the CoT extension and new benchmarks.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and Appendix A.1–A.10 remain unchanged. v3 inserts CoT subsections, additional benchmark sections, limitations and two appendix sections while preserving the original narrative sequence. Wording and cross-reference edits are limited rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds a first-page system overview, expands Table 1 with baseline and CoT rows, and introduces Tables 2–4. Appendix figures 4–5 present website statistics and training/inference settings as tables. The original two diagrams are retained as Figures 2–3. These additions substantially expand the visual presentation beyond renumbering and pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation through full-WebArena and real-world WebVoyager experiments, while Appendix A.12 fills important reproducibility gaps. Expanded comparisons and explicit limitations also make the contribution easier to assess. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including the incorrect CoT-gain arithmetic and the conclusion's outdated treatment of executor CoT as future work. Sparse evaluation details for the new benchmarks and absent uncertainty estimates still limit confidence in the strongest performance claims.
